findings.title: Source of truth for rules and skills is ambiguous, with a hidden dependency on Claude output
findings.description:
The file layout says instruction files come "from `.claude/rules/typescript.md`" and prompts "from `.claude/skills/commit.md`". Elsewhere the doc says "source rules → compiled Copilot files" and that the script "understands the project-documents layout".

If the backend really reads `.claude/`, then `cf init --ide copilot` on a fresh directory has nothing to translate, because `setup-ide claude` never ran. That breaks the plan's criterion that the fresh-directory flow generates instructions and prompts, for exactly the driver user who no longer uses Claude.

The design should state that the copilot backend reads the same guide-side sources the claude backend reads, and should not label inputs with `.claude/` paths.

findings.title: Guide-script backend, where most behaviour lives, is specified in one bullet
findings.description:
The plan rates this slice Med risk because of translation correctness, yet the design leaves these open:
- **Rule classification:** line 83 equates "`paths` absent" with "alwaysApply". The plan treats these separately: non-alwaysApply rules become instruction files, defaulting to `applyTo: "**"` when paths are omitted. A non-alwaysApply rule with no `paths` is undefined here.
- **`paths` forms:** the plan says the translator "must handle both forms". Only the multi-line form is shown, and nothing says how a bash script parses YAML frontmatter, including the inline `paths: [a, b]` form.
- **Skill-to-prompt frontmatter:** the plan lists the target fields (`name`, `description`, `argument-hint`, `agent`, `model`, `tools`). The design gives no mapping from skill frontmatter and no rule for fields with no equivalent.
- **Instruction-file fields:** `name` and `description` on generated instruction files are not addressed.

findings.title: Managed-marker safety covers only two of the four output locations
findings.description:
The check inspects `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md` only. The script also writes into `.github/instructions/` and `.github/prompts/`, where existing Copilot users commonly keep hand-written files. A user-authored `typescript.instructions.md` or `commit.prompt.md` would be overwritten with no prompt and no backup, which misses the plan criterion "existing unmanaged files prompts before overwriting (same safety as Claude path)".

Three related gaps:
- `propagateToWorktrees` copies both directories wholesale into each worktree with no stated rule for unmanaged files already there.
- The helper is named twice with different signatures: `isManagedCopilot(filePath)` at line 29 and `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)` at line 109.
- Whether generated instruction and prompt files carry the marker is not stated; it would have to sit after their YAML frontmatter.

findings.title: Guide-version skew can produce a silent success, and failure modes are not enumerated
findings.description:
The Risks section asserts that a submodule without a `copilot` case "will fail at the script step with a clear error", but nothing in the design makes that true. If the installed script exits 0 on an unknown argument, step 7 prints `IDE setup complete for copilot.` with no files written, which conflicts with the project's no-silent-fallback principle. Skew is the expected case, since the guide skip rule leaves existing installs on older guides.

The design should specify:
- A non-zero exit on unknown targets in the script, and a post-run check in CF that the expected outputs exist (or a guide capability check before running), with an error pointing to `cf guides update`.
- Behaviour when the script fails after step 4 has already moved user files to `.bak`.
- Behaviour when a registered worktree path is missing or a copy fails mid-propagation: abort or continue, and what is reported.

findings.title: `cf init --ide copilot` flow is declared "no change" without addressing the command-install step
Plan success criteria with no coverage in the design
findings.description:
- **Tool guide:** the plan requires `project-documents/user/tool-guides/copilot-vscode/setup-ide.md` be "referenced in slice design, promoted to a proper published tool guide if needed". The design never references it or makes the promotion decision. The file is currently a raw Q&A export with no frontmatter.
- **Translation tests:** every listed test is CLI-side. Nothing verifies paths→applyTo conversion, the always-on versus scoped split, or prompt generation, which are three of the plan's criteria. The design does not say where guide-script tests live.
- **Manual verification:** the criterion that a Copilot agent follows conventions from the generated files is absent.
- **Custom agents:** line 54 says "document the mapping", but no mapping appears.

findings.title: Always-on content will be loaded more than once
findings.description: Identical content goes to both `AGENTS.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, and the tool guide says VS Code treats both as always-on, so the rules enter context twice. In dual-write repos it also recognises `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules`. The plan mandates both files, so this is not a deviation, but the design should acknowledge the duplication.

findings.title: Stale generated files are not cleaned up
findings.description: When a rule or skill is removed or renamed at source, its previously generated `.instructions.md` or `.prompt.md` stays and keeps applying, in the root and in every propagated worktree. The managed marker would allow safe pruning of managed files with no source; the design should state whether this slice does that.
